archetype.name: Play-In Exit (unlucky breakout)
archetype.definition: A team that jumped from the league's basement to a top-eight net rating, played like a 53-win side, but lost enough close games to land at 44-38 and fall in the play-in.

report.headline: A 53-win margin, 44 wins, and the league's worst luck to show for it

recap.finish: 44-38, third in the Southeast; lost in the play-in
recap.body:
This was not the same franchise. A year after going 19-63 with the 29th-ranked offense, Charlotte finished 44-38 with the league's fifth-best offensive rating (119.4) and a Net Rtg of 5, eighth in the NBA. The site has it ninth of 30. By the way it actually played, it belonged comfortably in the playoff field. By its record, it was third in a tight Southeast behind Atlanta (46-36) and Orlando (45-37) and stuck in the play-in, where the season ended.

The arc split cleanly in two. After a 2-3 October, November went 4-11 and December 5-8, leaving the Hornets 11-22 at the turn of the year, which looked like more of the same. Then the defense showed up. Opponents scored 118.73 a game in November and 117.08 in December, then 106.12 in January, 106 in February and 104.8 in March. Over those months Charlotte went 11-6, 8-3 and 10-5 and was 40-36 by the end of March. The offense barely moved over the same stretch, so the turnaround came from the other end of the floor. A 9-game winning streak and a 7-game skid bracket how uneven the year was.

The identity was shooting and the glass. Charlotte took 48.7% of its shots from three (second in the league) and made 37.8% (third), and it rebounded better than almost anyone: REB % of 54 (second), ORB % of 30.5 (fourth), DRB % of 76.6 (third). The weak spots were possessions given away and possessions not taken. TOV % ranked 25th, Opp TOV % also 25th, and FT Rate 23rd. This team rarely got to the line, didn't force mistakes, and coughed up its own.

The wings graded an A, and Kon Knueppel carried them: 81 games, 2,551 minutes, 273 threes on 63.3 TS % and a team-best 8 Win Shares. Brandon Miller added 1,311 points. LaMelo Ball ran everything at a 32 USG %, with a 4.7 BPM and +6.3 On-Off. His 54.6 TS % was the least efficient among the high-usage starters. Moussa Diabaté was the quiet engine up front, with 635 rebounds, 65.3 TS % and a +10.7 On-Off, the best on the roster. Ryan Kalkbrenner finished at 76.2 TS %. The backcourt graded a C because Ball had little help: Sion James played all 82 games with a -2 BPM, and Coby White managed only 50.

What cost them the playoffs was the scoreboard in close games, not the talent. Charlotte's W vs Pt Diff of -9 ranked dead last in the league. Its +396 differential implies 53 wins, yet it won 44. Even the closing stretch fit the pattern: 6-4 over the last 10 with a +6.3 margin a game, losses to Boston, Detroit and Philadelphia mixed in.

highlights.title: Offense went from 29th to 5th
highlights.body: Last season's ORtg was 107.3; this season's was 119.4, fifth in the league. It was built on volume and accuracy from three, with a 3PA Rate second in the NBA and 3P % third. Knueppel and Miller supplied a large share of that shooting. With both young wings carrying the A-graded group, the shooting looks repeatable rather than a hot streak.

highlights.title: Dominant on the glass
highlights.body: A REB % of 54 ranked second, and Charlotte owned both ends of the boards. Diabaté was central, with 635 rebounds and the roster's best On-Off. Opposing centers grabbed fewer rebounds against Charlotte than anyone else allowed, and fewer than in their own other games. With Kalkbrenner also efficient inside, the frontcourt's B grade undersells how much it shaped games.

highlights.title: Defense flipped after New Year
highlights.body: Opponents scored 118.73 a game in November, then 104.8 in March, and the record swung with it. Over the full season the DRtg of 114.4 ranked 12th, so the early months drag down what the defense became. The second-half version is the one that played like a playoff team.

lowlights.title: Worst close-game luck in basketball
lowlights.body: A W vs Pt Diff of -9 was 30th of 30. The differential pointed to 53 wins and the record delivered 44, the difference between a top-four seed and the play-in. Close-game results mostly even out, so this is the least likely problem to repeat. It still cost them this season.

lowlights.title: Lost the possession battle
lowlights.body: Charlotte turned it over at a 25th-ranked rate and forced turnovers at a 25th-ranked rate, and its FT Rate was 23rd. The rebounding edge won back possessions that the turnover gap gave away. Unlike the luck, this is structural and needs fixing.

lowlights.title: Thin backcourt behind Ball
lowlights.body: The backcourt graded a C, the roster's weakest group. Sion James started every game at 79th of 144 on the shooting-guard tab with a -2 BPM. Coby White's scoring came in only 50 games, and Ball himself was inefficient for his usage.

arc.note: Charlotte sat at 11-22 after December, then posted winning records in every month from January on behind a defense that gave up about 12 fewer points a game than in November. It finished 44-38.

recap.nextYear: The underlying team is far better than the record. A +396 differential and an eighth-ranked Net Rtg are what carry forward, while the -9 in close games is the part most likely to swing back. The core that produced it is young and productive. Knueppel (8 Win Shares, 63.3 TS %) and Miller anchor an A-graded wing group, Ball drives the offense, and Diabaté and Kalkbrenner give the frontcourt efficiency and rebounding. The work is in the backcourt beside Ball, the C-graded group, and in the possession game, where bottom-six turnover and free-throw ranks leave points on the table. If the defense from January through March holds for a full season and the close games split evenly, this profile points to a playoff seed rather than a play-in.

confidence.note: Full 82-game season with a stark luck signal; no play-in game detail in the sheet.
